memos.risk:
Risk officer read: this is a weak setup for a new buy, and I'd refuse entry.

Key facts: the coin is down 61.5% over 30 minutes and sits 69% below its 30-minute high, so it has already dumped hard. Its 15-minute return is +141%, but that is a short bounce off the low, not a trend. Pool depth is only 47.85 SOL, so a $20 round trip with 1.4-5.1% costs plus thin-pool impact is a real drag. Sellers (59) outnumber buyers (87) in the last 15 minutes, and net flow is positive only because of a few large buys.

Sizing if the desk overrides me: $5 ticket, 25% stop, 30-minute hold.

Refusal triggers: any further pool-depth decline, a sell-to-buy ratio above 1.0 in the next window, or a bundle share rising above 0.24.
memos.scout:
The strongest case for buying is the last 15 minutes: net flow was positive (+17.82 SOL), 87 buyers came in, and the price returned +40.7% over that window, so something is still pulling buyers in. The curve looks organic rather than operator-run: top-3 share is only 7.6%, the first two minutes after graduation had 486 distinct buyers and a top-5 buyer share of 17.7%, and the sell-to-buy ratio of 1.07 is not a dump signature. The bundle share (24%) is a yellow flag, but it is not extreme.

The case is weak, though. The coin is down 69% from its 30-minute high and down 62% over 30 minutes, so the recent bounce is a rebound inside a steep decline. The 15-minute window also had 59 sellers against 87 buyers and 23.97 SOL of sells, so the buying is thin. Pool depth of 48 SOL is shallow relative to a $20 ticket, and a round trip costs 1.4-5.1%. Coins in this state usually don't hold a bounce for long, and the base rate for buys this age is roughly a 20% loss per trade.

My honest read: there is a demand signal, but not enough to outweigh the base rate and the drawdown. Skip unless the desk wants a lottery-style bet.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss here is a dead-volume fade after a 69% drawdown from the 30-minute high. The last 15 minutes show buys of 41.79 SOL against sells of 23.97 SOL, but the 1.41 return is a snapback, not a trend: the coin is still down 61.5% over 30 minutes, and at a 47.85 SOL pool depth a $20 round trip at 1.4-5.1% cost barely moves unless the price rallies several times over. Early flow looks inorganic: a launch bot was present, and the sell-to-buy ratio of 1.07 in the first two minutes after graduation means early buyers were already exiting. The 24% bundle share on the curve and 30% completer share suggest coordinated accumulation that could distribute into any bounce. A bounce that stalls will bleed on fees. Skip.
